answer: Fake identity is beaten by cost, not cleverness. Every answer is an echo signed by one address, and the ledger seats only addresses whose rewards were attested by four peers across a full epoch. To mint a Sybil persona an attacker must fund it, survive the settlement delay, and pay attestation on real work; a saffron badge bought that way costs the same as honest labor, and a jetty of borrowed keys collapses the whole set the moment one signature mismatches.
